title: Genoa Peak Off Road Trail
summary: Christian drove the dirt road from the Kingsbury trailhead up to Genoa Peak with Marley scouting ahead, then down toward Spooner Lake. After an earlier trip where he couldn't make the last stretch on foot, this time he walked all the way to the top.

fieldNotes:
Went off roading from Kingsbury Zinger trail head up to Genoa Peak and then down to near Spooner lake and the highway 50. The tracker was left on a bit and some of the highway is at the end. Not a big deal. Marley was with me and she ran along for a bit. She love to scout ahead of the truck. The trail was nice and dry, a bit dusty but very pretty. I had been up in the truck before but could not walk the last few hundreds of feet up to the very top due to medical issues. Those issues were resolved and today was the first time I actually made it all the way to the top.

Are you comfortable mentioning the earlier health issues, even this vaguely, in both the post and the episode?
Sure. It has been addressed. Back pain and knee pain.

post.title: All the way to the top of Genoa Peak
post.body:
I started early, a little after seven thirty, at the Kingsbury trailhead and pointed the truck up the dirt road toward Genoa Peak. The plan was simple: up to the peak, then down the other side toward Spooner Lake and Highway 50.

Marley came along. She ran next to the truck for part of the way, and she loves to scout ahead, trotting out in front like she's checking the road for me.

The road was dry, a bit dusty, and very pretty. It winds through tall pines, and every so often the trees open up and you look straight down onto Carson Valley and Genoa, a long way below. I stopped a few times just to take that in, and to take a couple of selfies with the truck, because a break doesn't count unless you document it.

I've been up this road in the truck before. That time I couldn't walk the last few hundred feet to the very top because of back pain and knee pain. That's been taken care of now, and today I parked, got out and walked it. All the way up.

The top is a pile of broken rock with a view in every direction. Carson Valley spreads out on one side, Lake Tahoe sits on the other, and the ridges roll off between them. I stood there for a while.

From the peak I took the road down toward Spooner Lake. By the numbers it was about ten miles, around 2,500 feet of climbing and closer to 3,000 feet down, with the high point just over 9,100 feet. Moving time was about an hour and a half; the whole outing took about two and a half hours.

And yes, I left the tracker running again. Some of the highway ended up on the end of the track before I noticed. Not a big deal; it's trimmed off.

What I learned: a place you've already been can still have a first time left in it. The view from the truck was nice. The view after walking those last few hundred feet was something else.

episode.title: The last few hundred feet
episode.script:
Narrated by GlazyArray.

It was a little after seven thirty in the morning at the Kingsbury trailhead, and the light was still coming up over the pines.

Christian wasn't on a bike this time. He was in his truck, pointed up a dry dirt road toward Genoa Peak. And he wasn't alone. Marley was with him.

Marley has a job on these drives, and she takes it seriously. She ran alongside for a while, and then she did what she loves best. She scouted ahead of the truck, out in front, checking the road as if he'd hired her for it.

***

The road was dusty, but it was beautiful. Tall pines, soft dirt, and every so often a gap in the trees where the whole of Carson Valley lay down below, pale and wide in the morning haze. Christian stopped to look. He has a good eye for those gaps, the ones where the branches frame the valley just right, and he didn't rush past them.

Here's the part that matters. Christian had been up this road before. That time, he couldn't walk the last few hundred feet to the very top. His back and his knees wouldn't let him.

That had been taken care of. So this time, he parked, got out, and walked it.

All the way to the top.

***

The summit of Genoa Peak is a jumble of broken rock, just over nine thousand feet up. On one side, Carson Valley. On the other, Lake Tahoe, blue and quiet. Ridges rolling off in between. He took a picture of himself up there, sunglasses on, the whole view at his back. It's a modest little selfie. It's also a first.

Then it was back to the truck and down the other side, toward Spooner Lake and the highway. About ten miles in all, roughly twenty-five hundred feet up and three thousand down, in about two and a half hours.

And the tracker? Of course it was still running when he hit the highway. I'll say no more than that.

***

Some places you visit once. Some you have to visit twice, because the first time, the top was waiting for you to be ready. This was the second time.

blocks.title: Know before you go
blocks.text:
This is a point-to-point drive: up from the Kingsbury trailhead to Genoa Peak, then down the other side toward Spooner Lake and Highway 50.

On this October morning the road was dry and a bit dusty, winding through tall pines with openings that look straight down onto Carson Valley and Genoa.

The very top is the last few hundred feet on foot from where the truck parks, and the summit itself is a pile of broken rock.

Stop the tracker before you hit the highway.
